r.정치 구도: Papua New Guinea is a parliamentary democracy with the British monarch as head of state, and it gained independence from Australia in 1975. Its 118-seat parliament is split among dozens of parties and independents, so coalitions are fragile and attempts to topple the prime minister through no-confidence votes are constant. That is why the constitution bars no-confidence votes for 18 months after an election. In the highlands, tribal fighting is frequent and guns are widespread, leaving the state's reach weak. In a 2019 referendum, more than 97% of voters on Bougainville chose independence, and a tug-of-war continues over whether parliament will accept the result and when independence would take effect.

t.why: Lying just north of Australia, it is the largest Pacific island country by both population and land. As the former colonial power, Australia is its biggest aid donor. As China expanded its reach in the Pacific, Australia and the United States moved quickly to deepen security ties with Papua New Guinea. It signed a defense cooperation agreement with the United States in 2023, and in July 2026 the Pukpuk Treaty, a mutual defense pact with Australia, came into force. It is the country's first alliance and Australia's first new alliance in more than 70 years. Large liquefied natural gas projects and gold and copper mines keep it in resource news, and it became a focus of human rights controversy when Australia held asylum seekers who arrived by boat on Manus Island.
t.rel: It shares the island of New Guinea with Indonesia and is close to Australia, with which it signed a mutual defense treaty in 2025.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in May 1976 and marked the 50th anniversary in 2026. In trade, South Korea buys far more from Papua New Guinea than it sells. In December 2025 they signed a framework agreement on grant aid, which allows the Korea International Cooperation Agency to reopen its office in the capital, Port Moresby, after 14 years.
t.know: With more than 800 languages, it has more languages than any other country.
etext: Exports of liquefied natural gas since 2014 have greatly expanded the economy. A second large gas project is in preparation, but the final investment decision keeps slipping.

Several large gold and copper mines account for a big share of exports. The government is seeking bigger stakes in the mines to keep more of the revenue, which has led to tough bargaining with foreign companies.
Most people live in rural areas and farm. It exports palm oil, coffee and cocoa.

Resource income has not turned into many jobs, so few people have seen their lives improve in line with growth. Roads and power are scarce, businesses often struggle to get foreign currency on time, and insecurity holds back investment.
